title: SolarWave POC: Security, Benchmarks, and Success Criteria
next_steps: Maya to send SOC 2 + ISO27001 evidence pack and network diagram
Liam to propose benchmark plan (datasets, qps targets, latency SLOs) and resource estimate
Priya to share expected PII/data residency constraints and timeline for pilot sign-off
action_items: Maya Chen: Upload security binder + cert extracts by 2025-08-22
Liam O'Connor: Draft benchmark script and run plan by 2025-08-26

summary: Discovery and POC scoping for a 6-week pilot focusing on security/compliance posture and performance benchmarks. Customer requires SOC 2 and ISO27001 evidence, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC for admin/user roles, and detailed audit logs. Success criteria: pass security review, meet 95th percentile latency SLO (~200ms for short chat queries) and throughput target of 80 concurrent sessions / ~12k tokens/min with acceptable cost profile. Next steps include sending security artifacts, a benchmark plan, and sample data characteristics.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-19 09:00 PDT | Duration: ~52 minutes | Recording ID: ff-20250819-8732-solarwave-poc
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Priya Malhotra (SolarWave CTO), Daniel Brooks (ML Engineer), Marcus Lee (IT Security)
Shared links: Security binder (redacted): https://redwood.share/security-binder, Benchmark sheet (draft): https://redwood.share/benchmarks/sheet-24871

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro — I'm Maya, AE on this account, and Liam is our SE. Priya, Daniel, Marcus, thanks for making time.
[00:18] Priya Malhotra: Morning. We'll focus on the pilot scope, security requirements, and what kind of benchmarks we need to validate cost/latency. We have a tight regulatory window so details matter.
[00:34] Liam O'Connor: Great, I'll kick off with how we typically run the POC then dig into security plumbing. High level — 4 to 6 week pilot, two phases: security/setup and benchmark/validation.
[00:50] Daniel Brooks: For the workload — mostly chat-like customer prompts and some document reranking. Typical prompt length ~40-100 tokens, doc rerank uses 512 token contexts.
[01:07] Marcus Lee: From security: SOC 2 Type II is a hard requirement, ISO27001 preferred, and we need SSO via SAML, RBAC for admin/engineer roles, audit logs with user action + model responses, and KMS-managed encryption. Also we need data residency in our EU tenant for any EU customer PII.
[01:34] Maya Chen: Understood. We have SOC 2 report and ISO attestation excerpts in the binder I referenced — will send full cert extracts. We support SAML for SSO; Liam can walk through the RBAC model and what audit log fields we emit.
[01:50] Liam O'Connor: Quick note on hosted vs dedicated — if data residency or PII is a blocker you can run the pilot in Dedicated or Private. Dedicated gives you reserved GPUs and customer isolation, Private gives the full VPC/on-prem control and KMS/HSM options. For the pilot we typically do a Dedicated pool in the EU region to meet residency.
[02:15] Priya Malhotra: Cost is a concern too — we need to show unit economics. We'll want a benchmark that reflects peak concurrencies during billing cycles.
[02:29] Daniel Brooks: Peak is about 80 concurrent sessions, average turn length 6 messages, say 12k tokens per minute. Latency target: p95 under 300ms for short interactions, ideally 200ms. Also for reranking p95 under 1s.
[02:51] Liam O'Connor: Noted. For those numbers we'll recommend quantized model variants and warm KV cache for heavy reranking flows. We'll add an explicit KV prefix hit-rate measurement to the benchmark plan.
[03:07] Marcus Lee: On audit logs — we need immutable logs with: timestamp, user id, request hash, model id/version, tokens in/out counts, latency, and a checksum. Also retention policy 7 years for certain records. Can you support that?
[03:27] Maya Chen: We emit audit trails at route/token level and can extend fields. Retention is configurable in Dedicated/Private. Hosted has 90–365 day retention for standard tiers but we can offer extended retention as an add-on.
[03:46] Priya Malhotra: Any third-party attestations around key management? We prefer HSM-backed keys.
[03:54] Liam O'Connor: We integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault) and can support HSM-based keys if you deploy in Private or Dedicated with customer-managed keys. For hosted we use our own KMS but we have BYOK options for enterprise.
[04:12] Daniel Brooks: For the benchmark itself, can you run both throughput and quality checks? We want to make sure quantization doesn't degrade metrics like Rouge or BLEU where applicable and our own NPS for customer responses.
[04:28] Liam O'Connor: Yes — plan includes latency/throughput, token cost per 1k tokens, and quality regressions on a holdout eval set. We'll capture top-k output diffs and a simple rating script.
[04:42] Priya Malhotra: Timeline? We have a vendor selection window in 6 weeks. So pilot needs to complete and security review done within 4–5 weeks ideally.
[04:54] Maya Chen: We can compress to four weeks if requirements are clear and test data arrives quickly. Typical schedule: week 0 (kickoff + infra + SAML setup), week 1–2 (benchmark runs & tuning), week 3 (security review + extended logging), week 4 (final report & decision).
[05:12] Marcus Lee: For SAML we require 2FA enforcement on IdP and SCIM for provisioning — can you do SCIM?
[05:22] Liam O'Connor: Yes, we support SCIM for user provisioning. 2FA is enforced at the IdP level, Redwood is IdP-agnostic. We'll request metadata and ACS URLs.
[05:34] Daniel Brooks: About telemetry: we need to capture model inputs for debugging but PII must be redacted. How do you handle redaction?
[05:44] Maya Chen: We offer configurable redaction at ingest, token-level masking, and you can route raw logs to your VPC in Private deployments. For Hosted we provide anonymization hooks and can purge samples on request.
[05:58] Priya Malhotra: Good. For success criteria, here's what we propose — security checklist passed by Marcus, p95 latency <= 250ms for chat, throughput 10–13k tokens/min sustained, reranking p95 <= 1s, and no quality regression >3% on our eval metric. Acceptable cost is below $X per 1k tokens — I'll add exact target in follow-up.
[06:25] Liam O'Connor: That is reasonable. We'll include cost estimates across quantization levels and a fallback plan if latency or quality misses.
[06:35] Marcus Lee: On legal/compliance: we need contract language around breach notification 48 hours, SOC 2 attestation in contract, SSAE addendum, and an option for on-prem deployment if regs change.
[06:47] Maya Chen: We can surface those clauses in the enterprise term sheet. For the pilot contract we'll add an appendix that references SOC 2 attestation and breach notification SLAs.
[06:58] Speaker 1: [crosstalk] quick question on benchmarking dataset size —
[07:02] Daniel Brooks: We plan to provide 5k chat examples and 2k document pairs for rerank. Can you run those with synthetic traffic at target QPS?
[07:13] Liam O'Connor: Absolutely — we'll run deterministic replay, scale to your QPS and measure p50/p95/p99 latencies. We'll also simulate cold-starts and cache-warm scenarios.
[07:25] Priya Malhotra: For encryption in transit, TLS plus mTLS for service-to-service?
[07:31] Liam O'Connor: TLS everywhere by default; mTLS available in Private deployments.
[07:36] Marcus Lee: Logging format: JSON lines with schema. We need field names so our SIEM can ingest. Can you provide schema?
[07:44] Maya Chen: We'll attach a sample log schema. Liam will follow up with the exact field list (and we can add custom fields).
[07:52] Daniel Brooks: A tricky thing — some of our prompts contain financial PII. Can the KV cache be disabled for those flows?
[07:59] Liam O'Connor: Yes — prefix-based KV caching rules can be set per-route. You can opt out for sensitive routes.
[08:07] Priya Malhotra: What about model rollback and canarying? We may want to test a quantized variant in canary for say 5% of traffic.
[08:16] Liam O'Connor: We support canary rollouts and split traffic rules. We'll include rollout policy in the pilot plan.
[08:25] Maya Chen: Quick check — Marcus, you'll own security sign-off; Priya owns business sign-off; Daniel owns model/quality metrics?
[08:33] Marcus Lee: Yes, I'll lead security sign-off.
[08:36] Priya Malhotra: I'll handle acceptance criteria.
[08:39] Daniel Brooks: I'll validate quality metrics.
[08:41] Maya Chen: Great. Now I'll go through the benchmark plan high level.
[08:45] Liam O'Connor: Plan sections: infra footprint (GPU types, node counts), workload generator config, eval metrics (latency, throughput, quality), KV cache hit-rate, quantization variants (8-bit, 4-bit), and cost/slot math.
[09:05] Priya Malhotra: GPU type preference? We prefer Ampere or equivalent.
[09:10] Liam O'Connor: We recommend A10/A30 for a balanced cost/latency profile, A100 for heavy throughput. For quantized 4-bit variants A10 can perform well with our optimized kernels.
[09:20] Daniel Brooks: Can you provide an estimate of node count to reach 12k tokens/min at our target latency?
[09:27] Liam O'Connor: Rough estimate: with a quantized gpt-like backbone we'd expect 2-3 A10 nodes for steady 12k tokens/min with p95 ~200–300ms, but we'll run the exact sizing in the bench plan. We'll also measure cold-start tail.
[09:39] Priya Malhotra: For EU residency — can logs be routed to our EU tenant?
[09:43] Maya Chen: Yes, Dedicated/Private can route logs to your EU S3/Blob with lifecycle policies. Hosted's logs live in region but custody stays with Redwood unless BYOK.
[09:55] Marcus Lee: Any known limitations on exportable fields due to PII?
[09:59] Liam O'Connor: We can redact or hash PII fields. We'll show examples in the binder.
[10:07] Daniel Brooks: Benchmark acceptance tests — what does pass/fail look like?
[10:12] Liam O'Connor: Pass means meeting all defined SLOs in the bench doc: latency SLO, throughput target sustained for X minutes, quality regression <3%, and security checklist closed. If any hard security items fail, pilot is paused.
[10:26] Priya Malhotra: What about cost modeling? We need a per 1k token line item across options.
[10:33] Maya Chen: We'll provide a cost matrix for hosted/dedicated/private and variants (8-bit/4-bit) plus expected monthly run-rate at your projected QPS.
[10:41] Marcus Lee: One more on audit logs — we need tamper-evident chaining or signature for critical events. Can you do signed logs?
[10:49] Liam O'Connor: In Private you can ship logs to your HSM for signing. In Dedicated we can optionally sign logs with customer-managed keys. Hosted has signatures using our key management but we can include integrity proofs in the enterprise contract.
[10:59] Speaker 2: [laughter] that's a lot of paperwork, but necessary.
[11:03] Maya Chen: Final recap — deliverables from Redwood: security binder + cert snippets, benchmark plan & scripts, sizing estimate, sample audit log schema, and a pilot schedule. From SolarWave: sample datasets (anonymized or synthetic), SAML metadata/SCIM details, and acceptance thresholds.
[11:22] Priya Malhotra: We'll aim to get those over this week.
[11:26] Marcus Lee: I'll review the security binder and follow-up on any gaps.
[11:30] Daniel Brooks: I'll coordinate the dataset prep and share the eval metric.
[11:36] Maya Chen: Thanks all — we'll follow up with calendar invites for kickoff and send the security pack by Friday.
[11:44] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard acronyms (SAML sometimes transcribed as "sam el"), proper nouns slightly off (A10/A30 sometimes as A ten/A thirty), and timestamps are approximate.
